title: Activation funnel playbook: first-run pathways for SDKs, samples, and quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a repeatable playbook and tracked initiative to reduce 'time-to-first-success' for new developers using Redwood SDKs, sample apps, and quickstarts. Goal is to map existing first-run pathways, identify key friction points, and deliver 6 prioritized changes (docs, SDK samples, CLI flows, and one-click Console templates) with measurable lift in activation metrics.

Background: Despite healthy sign-ups, we see dropoff between API key creation and first successful generation/embedding call. Fragmented sample apps and inconsistent quickstart language cause confusion across JavaScript, Python, and Go SDKs. This initiative ties into OKR DX-2026-Q2 (Improve developer activation and retention).

Objectives and success criteria: 
- Objective 1: Reduce median time-to-first-success from 22 minutes -> <= 8 minutes for new SDK signups within 60 days of launch.
- Objective 2: Increase first-week active rate (FWA) by +12% for users following quickstarts.
- Objective 3: Achieve >75% completion of the guided quickstart in Console for new hosted API users.

Key deliverables: 
1) First-run pathway map (JS/Python/Go + Console + CLI) and friction heatmap.
2) Playbook doc with prioritized interventions (content + code + product) and acceptance criteria.
3) Updated canonical quickstarts: JS sample app, Python notebook, and minimal Go example.
4) One-click Console quickstart template and telemetry hooks for funnel tracking.
5) SDK starter template repository and automated smoke tests.
6) Measurement dashboard (Amplitude + Redash) and A/B experiment design.

Measurement plan: Track events: key_created, sample_repo_cloned, first_api_call_success, quickstart_completed, first_response_latency, billing_token_generated. AB test: current quickstart vs streamlined template. Success tracked in Amplitude cohort and monthly rollup in PM dashboard.

Acceptance criteria: Each prioritized change must have a rollout checklist, automated smoke test, and a dashboard signal. The playbook must include rollback criteria and owner for each change.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Investment in multiple language samples increases short-term work but expected to reduce support tickets.
- Console one-click templates require limited backend changes (early dependency: Console infra team).

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence baseline map: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEVX/pages/FR-Pathways-2026
- Draft playbook (internal): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Qk_devx_playbook
- SDK starter repo (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter-templates/pull/87
- Amplitude plan: https://analytics.amplitude.com/redwood/activation-playbook-2026

Stakeholders: DX PMs (owner), SDK engineering leads (implementation), Console & Console infra (templates), Docs (content), Solutions engineering (customer trials).
